blocks.text: Manuel Antonio to Bahía Ballena and Marino Ballena National Park

After breakfast, travel to Bahía Ballena.

From here, set out on a boat tour through Marino Ballena National Park that combines wildlife watching with coastal sightseeing.

Watching for marine wildlife is the main focus of the trip.

Look out for humpback whales, Pacific spotted dolphins, bottlenose dolphins, sea turtles and seabirds such as pelicans, frigatebirds and brown boobies.

Humpback whale sightings are seasonal.

The best time to see Southern Hemisphere humpbacks is from July to the end of October. They migrate from Antarctica to the coast of Costa Rica to breed and raise their calves.

Northern Hemisphere humpbacks travel from the waters off California and Washington State. The viewing season runs from late December to late February.

Whale sightings depend on the season and natural conditions.

With luck, you may hear whales sing or see them breach or lift their tails above the water.

The boat passes the natural formation known as the Whale’s Tail.

It also passes Ventanas Beach, where the ocean has carved sea caves into the rock.

Depending on the tide, the group makes a short stop at either Ventanas Beach or Arco Beach.

Fresh fruit is served during the stop.

You’ll spend the day exploring the scenery of Costa Rica’s southern Pacific coast.

Breakfast is included.

The tour ends here.
